notes: official register id=DK020; Purpose=Capacity development / training; Priority Areas=Enhanced knowledge and participation in Food System Transformation, increased resilience and sustainability of SHF practices, improved market access and post-harvest management; Beneficiary=Smallholder farmers; End Date=2027-11-30T00:00:00; Project Description=The project, "Reducing Food Loss and Waste (FLW) and Building Climate Resilience Among Smallholder Farmers in South Africa," is a two-year initiative designed to strengthen the adaptive capacity, livelihoods, and market participation of smallholder farmers (SHFs) through agroecology, improved post-harvest systems, and food system transformation. South Africa loses an estimated 10.3 million tonnes of food annually, much of it at primary production level—a burden that falls disproportionately on SHFs who rely on rain-fed farming, have limited storage and market access, and face increasingly severe climate shocks. Recognizing this, the project positions SHFs at the centre of climate adaptation and FLW reduction by equipping them with climate-smart practices, improved post-harvest methods, and reliable market pathways. Central project activities will focus on Mpumalanga, where 450 SHFs will be supported through training, demonstration sites, and market facilitation. Complementary baseline studies on FLW will be conducted in the Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, and the Western Cape to establish national insights into hotspots, farmer practices, and opportunities for scaling. Working through strong multisector partnerships—including the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform, and Rural Development (DALRRD), the Consumer Goods Council of South Africa (CGCSA), the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), FoodForward SA, and local cooperatives—the project ensures policy alignment, technical sophistication, and pathways for scaling.

The aim is to develop a prototype 'all-African' sodium-ion battery cell, made from raw materials sourced within South Africa, including vanadium for the cathode and biochar for the anode.
